issue_results.result: Confirmed; Major retained for the false class identity and its explicit use in the main-scope reduction.
issue_results.source_and_quantifiers: Physical pp3-4 and26-28. Definition6.1(ii) allows unrestricted directed unions. Every Y_alpha group is virtually locally indicable: finite groups have a trivial finite-index subgroup, successor outputs impose VLI explicitly, and limit stages only unite classes. Theorem1.6 requires countability, membership in T_VLI, finite lcm and a conjugation-closed subfield K of C. Theorem1.7 directly invokes it.
issue_results.affine_witness_check: With a=(diag(1,-1,-1),(1/2,1/2,0)), b=(diag(-1,1,-1),(0,1/2,1/2)), direct affine multiplication gives c=ab=(diag(-1,-1,1),(1/2,0,-1/2)), a^2=T_(1,0,0), b^2=T_(0,1,0), c^(-2)=T_(0,0,1), and [a,b]=T_(1,-1,-1). The translation subgroup L=Z^3 is normal; four distinct linear parts and the quotient relations give precisely four cosets. Squaring their nontrivial representatives gives an odd nonzero coordinate, proving torsion-freeness. Conjugation inverts a^2 and b^2, so every map H=<a,b> to Z kills a and b. Thus H is finitely generated, nontrivial, VLI and not LI.
issue_results.membership_check: The first-coordinate action has image the infinite dihedral group and kernel <b^2,c^(-2)>=Z^2. Vertex preimages B=<b,z> and C=<c,y> are Klein-bottle groups, with common index-two edge group <y,z>. Normal forms prove H=B*_Z2 C. Identity and inversion HNN constructions from the trivial group build Z, Z^2 and the Klein-bottle groups. Inductively, P=H^(n-1), P x Z^2, P x B and P x C are obtained by the same HNN operations, and P x H=(P x B)*_(P x Z^2)(P x C). Every output is virtually free abelian, as required.
issue_results.finite_lcm_and_non_VLI_check: G=direct sum_(n>=1) H is countable, torsion-free and a directed union of permitted H^n, so G belongs to T_VLI and lcm(G)=1. Set K=Q. For a finite-index J, its normal core N has finite quotient Q0. The finitely generated H has only finitely many homomorphisms to Q0, so infinitely many coordinate restrictions equal rho. Choose m distinct such coordinates, where m is the exponent of rho(H), including m=1 for a trivial image. The genuine diagonal embedding h->(h,...,h) has quotient rho(h)^m=1, so N, hence J, contains H. Therefore no J is LI. This is an infinite-group argument, not a conclusion from finite arithmetic enumeration.
issue_results.counterevidence: The proof of Theorem1.6 on p27 already explicitly invokes direct-limit permanence of localizations and Atiyah properties. This is material support for a repair; permanence is not absent from the manuscript. It does not make the asserted identity T_VLI=Y true. The missing bridge is from the actual directed-union closure to the stated Y_alpha induction. No failure of an Atiyah conclusion, no failure of all finite-edge arguments, and no whole-paper invalidity are inferred.
issue_results.repair_check: Induction gives subgroup closure and increasing Y_alpha stages. A rank-bounding ordinal for the set of all finitely generated vertex/edge subgroups shows that Loc(Y) is closed under the allowed graph operation; it is also directed-union closed. Conversely Y and its local closure lie in T_VLI. Therefore T_VLI=Loc(Y). The report's permanence argument then describes how to use the author's direct-limit input before the stage induction. Ring-theoretic conclusions still depend on the stated subgroup dimension, regular-closure and localization inputs.
issue_results.severity: Major is tied to the false central class lemma and invalid reduction of the advertised main scope, even at finite lcm. The availability of a repair and absence of a main-theorem counterexample are explicitly preserved; they do not erase that demonstrated derivation error.

issue_results.check: For K=Q, i delta_e tensor delta_e - delta_e tensor i delta_e is nonzero in the rational tensor product, detected by rational coordinate functionals with value -1, but maps to zero under the complex-bilinear rank-one map. In the original formula alpha(v tensor u)(x)=<x,u*>v, the involution and Hermitian pairing do give complex bilinearity. This proves that a mechanical replacement of tensor_C by tensor_K is insufficient.
issue_results.boundary: The tensor is not shown to lie in a kernel of the diagonal Tor map. No counterexample to Tor vanishing, localization or the Atiyah conclusions is claimed. A coefficient-specific proof or an applicable descent argument remains a disclosed scientific limitation of the accepted bounded report.
